How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below you’ll find everything you need to hit the **“Get Information of Device Connector Versions”** API on a Cisco Nexus‑Dashboard instance running version 6.3.1 – whether you’re calling it manually with `cURL`, through a browser extension such as *Postman*, or programmatically with Python’s `requests` module. > ⚠️ > All examples assume your dashboard is reachable at `https://your-nexus-host`. Replace this placeholder with the actual hostname/IP address of your Nexus‑Dashboard appliance. --- ## 1️⃣ Authentication – Obtain a bearer token Cisco Nexus‑Dashboard uses OAuth‑style bearer tokens. First call `/auth/login` (or whatever login endpoint your deployment exposes) with your admin username/password. ```bash POST https://your-nexus-host/auth/login Content-Type: application/json { "username": "", "password": "" } ``` Typical response (`200 OK`) contains a field called `"access_token"`: ```json { "access_token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...", ... } ``` Save that value – you will prepend it with `Bearer ` when making subsequent calls. > 👉 If your environment requires HTTPS certificate validation, make sure the server presents a trusted cert. For quick testing you may add `--insecure/-k` to `cURL`. --- ## 2️⃣ Call the “Device Connector Versions” API ### 2a. Using `cURL` ```bash export TOKEN="eyJhbGc..."; # <-- paste the access_token here curl --silent --show-error \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \ https://your-nexus-host/api/v2/deviceConnectorVersions ``` *If you prefer verbose output:* replace `--silent` with `-v`. #### Expected Response (example) ```json [ { "id": 123, "name": "Connector A", "version": "7.0.1", "status": "active" }, { "id": 124, "name": "Connector B", "version": "8.2.3", "status": "deprecated" } ] ``` *(Your real payload will contain all connectors registered against the dashboard.)* --- ### 2b. Using Postman | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Create a new **GET** request → `https://your-nexus-host/api/v2/deviceConnectorVersions` | | 2 | Under **Headers**, set:
`Key`: `Accept` `Value`: `application/json`
`Key`: `Authorization` `Value`: `Bearer {{token}}` | | 3 | In the **Pre-request Script** tab, store the token if you fetched it earlier: ```pm.environment.set("token", pm.response.json().access_token);``` | | 4 | Hit **Send** | --- ### 2c. Programmatic call with Python (`requests`) ```python import json import requests BASE_URL = "https://your-nexus-host" LOGIN_ENDPOINT= "/auth/login" VERSIONS_EP = "/api/v2/deviceConnectorVersions" USERNAME = "admin_user" PASSWORD = "StrongPassword!" def fetch_access_token(): resp = requests.post( f"{BASE_URL}{LOGIN_ENDPOINT}", json={"username": USERNAME, "password": PASSWORD}, verify=False # remove or set True in production! ) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json()["access_token"] def list_device_connectors(token): headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Accept": "application/json"} r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}{VERSIONS_EP}", headers=headers, verify=False) r.raise_for_status() return r.json() if __name__ == "__main__": tok = fetch_access_token() data = list_device_connectors(tok) print(json.dumps(data, indent=2)) ``` > 🔒 **Security tip:** Never hard‑code passwords in scripts. Prefer environment variables or secret vaults. --- ## 3️⃣ Common Troubleshooting Tips | Symptom | Likely Cause & Fix | |---------|--------------------| | `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired or wrong. Re‑authenticate. | | `404 Not Found` | Wrong endpoint URI. Verify the API docs for v6.3.1. | | SSL errors | Self‑signed cert not trusted. Add `verify=false` (dev only) or import the CA into your client truststore. | | Rate limiting | Too many rapid requests. Respect back‑off headers returned by the API. | --- ## 4️⃣ Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Task | Command / Code Snippet | |------|-----------------------| | Login & capture token | See section 1 above | | List connectors | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://host/api/v2/deviceConnectorVersions` | | Parse JSON in Bash | `jq .` after piping the `curl` result | | Store token in env var (Bash) | `TOKEN=$(curl ... | jq -r '.access_token')` | Feel free to copy/paste the snippets directly into your terminal or IDE. Happy querying!
